reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not support the key premises. E1 describes a metallic HEA for nitrate reduction, not oxide formation or automotive exhaust catalysis. E2 describes a bulk spinel HEO for wet air oxidation of wastewater, not an in-situ formed overlayer on an alloy, and its conditions (high pressure, liquid phase) are unrelated to the proposed low-temperature gas-phase treatment. No evidence is provided for the specific oxidation treatment, the formation mechanism, or the performance under automotive exhaust conditions.
premises: Low-temperature oxidation (~300°C) of a multi-element alloy can form a conformal, ultrathin high-entropy oxide overlayer.
The oxide overlayer will be enriched in stable non-PGM metal oxides and have a spinel or perovskite-like structure.
The oxide overlayer passivates active sites, limits sintering and elemental dissolution, and optimizes oxygen vacancy populations.
The oxide overlayer facilitates effective adsorption/desorption of exhaust intermediates like NO and water, enhancing catalytic turnover.
The treatment will improve activity retention and durability under transient low-temperature exhaust conditions with H2O and NO.
